judgements.justification: B's AWCx (5, confidence 2) asked whether the power-cell Lloyd algorithm is a contribution, though the paper credits it to [11] and [14] and claims only the analysis; A's T7tc misread eq. (15) but its suspected typo did not drive its score, and no A reviewer made AWCx's error.
A's AC overstated the reviewers' view of the experiments, but the spotlight matches ratings 9/8/7/6 (mean 7.5); the chair followed the scores rather than setting a tier above them.
A's high ratings (u2eX 9, nnEq 8, both confidence 4) rest on detailed proof checks, not enthusiasm; B's light fudr 7 at confidence 3 did not carry B's decision.
Only on B's forum did the authors concede to Xcrv that an i.i.d. N-sample from rho 'achieves a better convergence rate'; A never saw this admission.

A learned that the method needs the density ('not studied yet') and that Theorem 7 is weaker than the one-step bound, yet accepted Theorem 7 on a promise of a future proof strategy, and its meta-review did not weigh these gaps.
In A, gM3z raised its score to 7 after the tightness reply; in B no score moved after the rebuttal.

Only B raised the missing comparison with an i.i.d. N-sample (Xcrv), the cost of computing power-cell barycenters (t3bd, AWCx) and the uncited gradient-flow claim, and B's AC built the rejection on these.

Both committees saw the gap to the optimal N^(-2/d), the weak Theorem 7, 2D-only experiments and the need for the density; A treated them as future work, B's AC as 'important aspects that are not treated'.

B's AC split ratings 6/7/5/5 by adopting Xcrv's i.i.d.-sample point and t3bd's cost point and did not weigh fudr's 7 or t3bd's 'close to being ready for publication'; stage 1 marks the meta-review as leaning on a specific reviewer.
t3bd cited 'issues raised by other reviewers' but kept its 6; no score moved because of the other reviews.
The authors did not answer Xcrv's follow-up on the uncited gradient-flow experiments, and Xcrv stayed at 5, the score the AC leaned on.
B's AWCx (5, confidence 2) restated the abstract, listed only minor items and posted nothing after the rebuttal, and its below-threshold rating counted in a split panel.
B's ratings 6/7/5/5 split two and two; the AC did not reject against a positive majority.
B's AC stated no positive view of the paper; it called the work 'too preliminary'.
Xcrv's 5 rests on the i.i.d.-sample comparison, which is central to what the result buys, and the authors conceded rather than answered it.
A read the paper as an explanation of why a non-convex method works; B read it as an approximation method and asked what it buys over sampling and at what cost.
gM3z (confidence 3) raised on the technical tightness argument and did not say the core was outside its expertise.
The difference is in what kind of contribution each committee read (R16), not two bars for one agreed kind.
A's overstatement of 'strong numerical contributions' came from the AC's meta-review, not from a reviewer's wrong claim behind a high score.
No below-threshold reviewer said its main concern was resolved; Xcrv's concern was conceded, not answered, and t3bd stayed at 6.
No record shows the authors promised B the sample comparison or a cost analysis; the difference is how the same gaps were weighted (R08).
No reviewer stated a changed position that its score did not reflect.
No late extra reviewer appears in either committee.
AWCx's 'not well-written' is a low-confidence complaint, but no A domain expert is on record reading the exposition as clear in contrast, and clarity did not drive B's decision.
AWCx edited its review without comment, but no raised rating against its own text is visible.
Neither AC set aside a silent detractor.

added.name: Invested champion present in one committee only
added.definition: One committee had a reviewer who rated the paper well above the acceptance threshold on a detailed, checked reading and argued for it, while the other committee had no reviewer rating it that high, so no one there advocated for acceptance.
added.justification: R03 covers a champion whose score rests on enthusiasm, not specifics; no reason names the opposite mechanism, a well-grounded advocate present in one committee and absent in the other, which here separates a 7.5 mean with two proof-checked high ratings from a 5.75 mean with none above 7.

reasoning: Stage 1 finds the committees weighted the same facts differently and that one correct point, the missing i.i.d.-sample comparison, reached only B, where the authors conceded it. That gives R04, R07, R08 and R16. The rebuttal moved gM3z in A only (R06). B's AC built the reject on Xcrv's and t3bd's points (R09), with Xcrv's follow-up unanswered (R11) and AWCx's thin 5 counted (R12, R01 for its wrong contribution claim). A accepted density access and Theorem 7 as future work on a promise (R05). The remaining asymmetry, two proof-checking champions rating 9 and 8 in A against no B rating above 7, has no existing reason, so R27 is added.
